{
  "IP": "neorv32_gpio",
  "Conceptual Assets": [
    {
      "Concept ID": "C1",
      "Concept Name": "Sampled GPIO input data",
      "Unit": "neorv32_gpio",
      "Information": "The sampled values received on the GPIO input pins are held for software reads and used by interrupt detection. The data enters through gpio_i and can be returned through the bus read-data path.",

        "Confidentiality": "yes",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "no",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Confidentiality is relevant because bus reads expose the sampled GPIO values through bus_rsp_o.data at line 83; integrity is relevant because port_in is overwritten from gpio_i at line 103 and the resulting value affects returned data and interrupt detection.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "C",
        "I"
      ],
      "Attack": "An unauthorized reader could use the GPIO input readback to disclose external data, or an attacker could spoof the GPIO input to alter the sampled value and interrupt behavior.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "gpio_i"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "bus_rsp_o.data"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        103
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        100,
        103
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        83
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C2",
      "Concept Name": "GPIO output value",
      "Unit": "neorv32_gpio",
      "Information": "The latched GPIO output value determines the levels driven on gpio_o and is also available through bus readback. GPIO operation depends on retaining the programmed output value.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "no",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Integrity is relevant because a bus write assigns port_out at line 74 and port_out directly drives gpio_o at line 112, so an unauthorized write can change external GPIO behavior.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I"
      ],
      "Attack": "An unauthorized bus write could overwrite the GPIO output value and drive incorrect levels on the external pins.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "bus_req_i.data"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "gpio_o",
        "bus_rsp_o.data"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        74
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        59,
        74
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        84,
        112
      ]
    },
    {

      "Information": "This transient decision identifies the configured GPIO level or transition that should create an interrupt. It is computed by irq_trigger and is captured into the pending interrupt state rather than exposed directly on a port.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Integrity and availability are relevant because irq_trig is computed from sampled GPIO values and trigger configuration at lines 125-129 and determines whether irq_pend is updated at line 141.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could spoof or suppress GPIO transitions, or corrupt the trigger decision, causing false or missing interrupt events.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "gpio_i"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [],
      "Entry Lines": [
        103
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        125,

        127,

        129

      "Exit Lines": []
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C4",
      "Concept Name": "Interrupt trigger mode and polarity",
      "Unit": "neorv32_gpio",
      "Information": "The trigger configuration selects whether each GPIO interrupt responds to a level or an edge and which polarity is recognized. Interrupt generation depends on these stored settings.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },

      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"

        "bus_req_i.data"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "bus_rsp_o.data"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [

        61,
        75,
        76
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        85,
        86
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C5",
      "Concept Name": "Interrupt enable mask",
      "Unit": "neorv32_gpio",
      "Information": "The per-GPIO interrupt enable mask controls which generated trigger events can become pending interrupts. It is stored as configuration and can be read back.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },

      "Held Lines": [
        62,

      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        87
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C6",
      "Concept Name": "Pending GPIO interrupt state and CPU request",
      "Unit": "neorv32_gpio",
      "Information": "The pending state records enabled GPIO interrupt events until they are cleared and produces the aggregate request sent to the CPU. CPU interrupt handling depends on preserving and correctly reporting this state.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Integrity and availability are relevant because irq_pend is reset and updated at lines 138-141, is returned through bus_rsp_o.data at line 88, and drives cpu_irq_o at line 142, so corruption or clearing can cause incorrect or missing CPU interrupts.",

        "I",
        "A"

        "gpio_i"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "bus_rsp_o.data",
        "cpu_irq_o"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        103
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        138,
        141
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        88,
        142
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C7",
      "Concept Name": "Interrupt clear mask command",
      "Unit": "neorv32_gpio",
      "Information": "The clear mask controls which pending GPIO interrupt bits are retained or cleared on the next update. It is a transient bus-controlled command used to modify the pending interrupt state and is not directly read back.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Integrity and availability are relevant because irq_clrn is loaded from bus write data at line 78 and participates in the pending-state update at line 141, allowing pending interrupts to be cleared or retained incorrectly.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An unauthorized bus write could supply a clear mask that prematurely clears required pending interrupts or prevents their clearing.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "bus_req_i.data"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [],
      "Entry Lines": [
        78
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        63,
        69,
        78
      ],
      "Exit Lines": []
    }
  ],
  "Not Kept": [
    {

      "Merged Into": "C3",
      "Why Not Kept": ""
    },

      "Candidate Name": "Bus access command fields and response handshake",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_gpio",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The address, direction and strobe fields are access-command information under the record-field rule, while the acknowledge and constant error response are bus-handshake information rather than independent assets."

    {

      "Merged Into": "",

    }
  ],
  "Notes": []
}

conceptual assets.information: The sampled values received on the GPIO input pins are held for software reads and used by interrupt detection. The data enters through gpio_i and can be returned through the bus read-data path.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is relevant because bus reads expose the sampled GPIO values through bus_rsp_o.data at line 83; integrity is relevant because port_in is overwritten from gpio_i at line 103 and the resulting value affects returned data and interrupt detection.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized reader could use the GPIO input readback to disclose external data, or an attacker could spoof the GPIO input to alter the sampled value and interrupt behavior.

conceptual assets.information: The latched GPIO output value determines the levels driven on gpio_o and is also available through bus readback. GPIO operation depends on retaining the programmed output value.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is relevant because a bus write assigns port_out at line 74 and port_out directly drives gpio_o at line 112, so an unauthorized write can change external GPIO behavior.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized bus write could overwrite the GPIO output value and drive incorrect levels on the external pins.

conceptual assets.information: This transient decision identifies the configured GPIO level or transition that should create an interrupt. It is computed by irq_trigger and is captured into the pending interrupt state rather than exposed directly on a port.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity and availability are relevant because irq_trig is computed from sampled GPIO values and trigger configuration at lines 125-129 and determines whether irq_pend is updated at line 141.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could spoof or suppress GPIO transitions, or corrupt the trigger decision, causing false or missing interrupt events.

conceptual assets.information: The trigger configuration selects whether each GPIO interrupt responds to a level or an edge and which polarity is recognized. Interrupt generation depends on these stored settings.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is relevant because bus writes load irq_typ and irq_pol at lines 75-76; availability is relevant because those settings select the trigger behavior used at lines 123-129 and can suppress or misdirect interrupt generation.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized bus write could change the trigger mode or polarity so required GPIO events are missed or spurious interrupts are generated.

conceptual assets.information: The per-GPIO interrupt enable mask controls which generated trigger events can become pending interrupts. It is stored as configuration and can be read back.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity and availability are relevant because a bus write assigns irq_en at line 77 and irq_en gates the pending-interrupt update at line 141, allowing interrupts to be altered or blocked.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized bus write could clear or set interrupt-enable bits, suppressing required CPU notifications or enabling unintended ones.

conceptual assets.concept: Pending GPIO interrupt state and CPU request
conceptual assets.information: The pending state records enabled GPIO interrupt events until they are cleared and produces the aggregate request sent to the CPU. CPU interrupt handling depends on preserving and correctly reporting this state.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity and availability are relevant because irq_pend is reset and updated at lines 138-141, is returned through bus_rsp_o.data at line 88, and drives cpu_irq_o at line 142, so corruption or clearing can cause incorrect or missing CPU interrupts.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter, clear, or prevent pending interrupt bits so the CPU receives a false interrupt status or misses a required interrupt.

conceptual assets.information: The clear mask controls which pending GPIO interrupt bits are retained or cleared on the next update. It is a transient bus-controlled command used to modify the pending interrupt state and is not directly read back.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity and availability are relevant because irq_clrn is loaded from bus write data at line 78 and participates in the pending-state update at line 141, allowing pending interrupts to be cleared or retained incorrectly.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized bus write could supply a clear mask that prematurely clears required pending interrupts or prevents their clearing.

considered, not kept.concept: Bus access command fields and response handshake
considered, not kept.reason: The address, direction and strobe fields are access-command information under the record-field rule, while the acknowledge and constant error response are bus-handshake information rather than independent assets.
The readback word is a selected copy of GPIO data or register contents at lines 83-88, so its information is covered by the underlying assets rather than forming an independent piece.
GPIO_NUM only fixes the elaborated width at build time and cannot be changed or withheld by the IP at run time.
